_notes: Concept prompts for the built things LocalSpawn makes (Hunyuan3D shape + UltraTex texture): stations, chests and
the pilot's whole Smithy. Same phases and keys as gathering_manifest.json (generate_gathering.py --group structures);
the models go to the 'art' folder and into the prefabs by AgentScripts/BuildStructureModels.cs.
Fires are made cold (no flames, no glow, no smoke): the game adds the flame, the light and the sparks.
Sod roofs are made bare (dark peat, no grass): the 3D model draws grass badly, and the builder grows the game's own
grass on the roof instead, so it is the meadow's grass in colour, wind and season.
A building is made to look like its concept image, not like the stand-in it replaces.
UltraTex (FLUX) is a non-commercial licence and Hunyuan3D's licence excludes some territories: re-texture/check before a release.
common: Three-quarter view from slightly above, whole object visible and centred, isolated on a plain light grey background. Matte, softly lit, no glow.

looks.prompt: A cold unlit campfire: a ring of nine rounded grey field stones, each the size of a loaf of bread, set close together around a bed of pale grey ash and black charcoal, with five short split birch logs, white bark and charred black ends, laid low in a star across the middle. No flames, no smoke, no embers.

A sturdy old Norse wooden sea chest, closed, with a slightly curved lid, thick weathered oak planks, three hammered black iron straps with round rivets running over the lid and down the front, an iron hasp with a ring lock in the middle of the front, and an iron carrying ring on each end.

A small old Norse village smithy, one long low building seen from outside, about twice as wide as it is tall: walls of dark weathered horizontal logs with notched corners on a foundation of rounded grey field stones; a low-pitched gable roof covered with a thick, lumpy layer of bare dark brown peat earth, with no grass, no plants and no moss growing on it, a peeled log along each eave holding the earth, pale birch bark showing under the roof's edges, and weathered bargeboards on the gables; a squat chimney of grey stones with a flat cap stone rising through the roof at one end; the long front side open under the eave between two timber posts with diagonal braces, showing a stone forge inside, with an iron anvil on a tree stump and a wooden quench barrel standing at the opening. No people, no fire, no smoke.
